Inspect and create seek's configuration: the client's, or with --server the server's. Never reads a secret.

Part of [`seek`](seek.md).

## Usage

```text
seek config [options] [command]
```

## Options

| Option | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-h, --help` | display help for command |  |

## Commands

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`seek config path`](seek-config-path.md) | Print the configuration file that seek config init writes. |
| [`seek config init`](seek-config-init.md) | Write a commented template of the configuration file, created with mode 0600. |
| [`seek config show`](seek-config-show.md) | Show each effective setting and the layer that supplied it; secrets appear as their redacted source. |
| [`seek config validate`](seek-config-validate.md) | Validate the configuration; exit 0 when it passes and 1 otherwise. |

## Exit statuses

`seek config` exits with one of the [exit statuses of `seek`](seek.md#exit-statuses).

## Help

The output of `seek config --help`:

```text
Usage: seek config [options] [command]

Inspect and create seek's configuration: the client's, or with --server the
server's. Never reads a secret.

Options:

Commands:

  init [options]      Write a commented template of the configuration file,
                      created with mode 0600.
  show [options]      Show each effective setting and the layer that supplied
                      it; secrets appear as their redacted source.
  validate [options]  Validate the configuration; exit 0 when it passes and 1
                      otherwise.
  help [command]      display help for command
```
